profile.name: Shuvro Ahmed
profile.role: Erasmus Mundus scholar · Imaging / Visual AI
profile.headline:
Computer vision.
A wider perspective.
profile.bio: I’m Shuvro, an Erasmus Mundus scholar in Imaging, on the Visual AI track. I’m currently at Mid Sweden University, following my first year at Politecnico di Milano.
profile.research_statement: My interests span visual representation learning, image and video understanding, and 3D vision. I’m interested in building learning systems that make sense of complex visual data—and understanding where those systems succeed or fail.
profile.personal_intro: Away from research, I enjoy travelling, cricket, and historical fiction. Studying across countries has also made discovering new places and meeting new people a meaningful part of my life.

research.title: Temporal learning for waste anomaly localization
research.summary: Extending a hierarchical VQ-VAE-2 with temporal bottom-code consistency, normal-code repair, and decoder adaptation for reconstruction-based anomaly localization.
research.question: Can information from consecutive normal frames improve anomaly localization without adding a new trainable network?
research.method: The working framework starts from a trained hierarchical VQ-VAE-2. During adaptation, current-frame bottom codes are encouraged to agree with reliable, detached matches from a previous normal frame. A normal-code frequency rule then supplies an alternative reconstruction path; decoder-only adaptation and bounded RGB blending are investigated as further stages.
research.evaluation: The study examines reconstruction-based localization and the effect of each adaptation stage. Comparative experiments and ablations focus on mean frame IoU, evaluation protocols, and failure cases.
research.limitation: Code frequency is not a complete model of semantic normality: rare desired material may be altered, while an unwanted object can still use familiar codes. Both reconstruction paths retain the same top-level context.
research.next: Continuing comparative experiments, ablations, and manuscript refinement, with particular attention to evaluation protocols and failure cases.
research.image_alt: Figure 1 from the working manuscript: temporal adaptation, normal-code repair, decoder adaptation, and single-frame inference with two shared-decoder paths.
research.caption: Temporal adaptation, normal-code repair, and single-frame inference. Figure 1, working manuscript.
research.manuscript_title: Temporal Code Consistency and Normal-Code Repair for Reconstruction-Based Waste Anomaly Localization

research.title: Perceptual quality of novel-view-synthesis videos
research.summary: Studying how local visual degradation and short low-quality intervals influence the agreement between objective quality metrics and human judgments of rendered videos.
research.question: To what extent can local and temporal pooling improve agreement between objective quality scores and human judgments of novel-view-synthesis videos?
research.method: The first stage compares conventional averaging with spatial-tail pooling and worst-window temporal pooling of existing quality metrics. Pooling settings are selected on training data rather than the test set. A second, exploratory stage considers a compact predictor using spatial image statistics, temporal signals such as optical flow or flicker, and optional learned features.
research.evaluation: The plan is to compare predictions with human quality ratings, using scene-disjoint evaluation to assess generalization and prevent views from the same scene leaking across training and testing. It also examines conditions where alternative pooling does not help.
research.limitation: The study will test whether emphasizing local defects and short low-quality intervals helps consistently across scenes, and where conventional averaging remains preferable.
research.next: Implementing the pooling study, examining agreement with subjective ratings, and determining whether a learned predictor is justified by the evidence.

projects.title: Pixel-level anomaly segmentation in multi-view images
projects.summary: A U-Net, DeepLabV3+, and SegFormer ensemble with synthetic anomaly generation and test-time augmentation.
projects.problem: Identify anomalous regions at pixel level in a multi-view image setting.
projects.approach: Combined U-Net, DeepLabV3+, and SegFormer models trained with real masks and synthetic anomalies. Flip and multi-scale test-time augmentation are followed by score-map fusion and post-processing.
projects.outcome: The final ensemble achieved a Pixel-AP of 0.9264 on the course challenge leaderboard.
projects.image_alt: Qualitative anomaly-localization output showing a reference image, real defect, ground truth, individual model maps, and the fused prediction.
projects.image_caption: Reference image, real defect, ground truth, and model outputs. Figure 4, ADL challenge report.

projects.title: Single-view 3D reconstruction of a ribbed cylindrical vault
projects.summary: Recovering vault geometry from one photograph using projective geometry, vanishing points, and geometric constraints.
projects.problem: Infer a three-dimensional architectural structure from a single two-dimensional view.
projects.approach: Used vanishing points, scene symmetries, and geometric constraints to calibrate the camera, rectify a cross-section, and recover points along a rib from a single photograph.
projects.outcome: Produced a single-view geometric reconstruction of the vault.
projects.image_alt: Annotated photograph of a ribbed vault with selected geometric lines used for single-view reconstruction.
projects.image_caption: Annotated input photograph showing the geometric features used for reconstruction. Figure 1, IACV report.

projects.title: Predicting municipal IFC with the GRINS dataset
projects.summary: Panel-aware LASSO and nested-region linear mixed-effects modelling for Italy’s municipal fragility index.
projects.problem: Predict municipal IFC from the GRINS data while accounting for repeated observations and regional structure.
projects.approach: Combined panel-aware variable selection with nested-region linear mixed-effects models. The model structure acknowledges that municipal observations do not form a simple independent sample.
projects.outcome: Reported cross-validated R²: 0.853.
projects.image_alt: Local spatial association maps of municipal employment in Italy, comparing 2018 and 2022.

projects.approach: Formulated route and coverage constraints, with exactly-once inspection and an objective involving drone return time.
projects.outcome: An optimization formulation for coordinated four-drone inspection routes.

projects.title: Pain-level classification from multivariate time series
projects.summary: CNN–BiGRU–Attention temporal modelling combined with LightGBM global motion features.
projects.problem: Classify pain levels from multivariate motion time series.
projects.approach: Combined a neural temporal model with global motion features processed by LightGBM. The two components capture complementary sequence-level and aggregate information.
projects.outcome: The final CNN–BiGRU–Attention and LightGBM ensemble achieved a macro-F1 of 0.9427 on the Kaggle course challenge.

projects.title: Molecular subtype classification from histopathology images
projects.summary: A three-seed EfficientNet-B0 ensemble with image/mask pairs, region-of-interest cropping, and test-time augmentation.
projects.problem: Classify histopathology images into four molecular subtypes.
projects.approach: Used image/mask pairs to form region-of-interest crops, followed by EfficientNet-B0 models trained with three seeds and combined using an ensemble and test-time augmentation.
projects.outcome: The three-seed ensemble with test-time augmentation achieved a public-leaderboard macro-F1 of 0.3784.

projects.title: Visual reconstruction of played piano music
projects.summary: Tracking hand landmarks and finger presses with MediaPipe to map fingertips to piano keys and reconstruct played notes.
projects.problem: Recover which notes are played from visual observations of piano performance.
projects.approach: Tracked hand landmarks and finger presses using MediaPipe, then mapped fingertip positions to piano keys to reconstruct the played note sequence.
projects.outcome: A vision-based pipeline connecting hand motion, key positions, and played notes.

projects.title: Physics-informed transfer learning for relative sea-level projections
projects.summary: Physics-informed modelling and cross-regional transfer learning for relative sea-level projections in Bangladesh, Vietnam, and the Maldives, with vertical land motion and coastal-vulnerability analysis.
projects.problem: Study regional relative sea-level projections for Bangladesh, Vietnam, and the Maldives, including differences in data availability and vertical land motion.
projects.approach: The manuscript combines an LSTM-based forecasting framework, cross-regional transfer learning, physics-informed training constraints, vertical-land-motion corrections, and SHAP-based analysis. It examines both historical prediction and longer-horizon projection behaviour.
projects.outcome: A manuscript on relative sea-level forecasting, transfer learning, and coastal vulnerability across Bangladesh, Vietnam, and the Maldives. Submitted and under review.

projects.title: Wildfire image classification with a convolutional Kolmogorov–Arnold network
projects.summary: A CNN–KAN hybrid for classifying satellite images as wildfire or no wildfire.
projects.problem: Distinguish wildfire from non-wildfire observations in satellite imagery.
projects.approach: Combined convolutional feature extraction with Kolmogorov–Arnold network layers and compared the model with convolutional baselines.
projects.outcome: The KAN–CNN achieved 97.32% test accuracy in the published study.

projects.title: Forecasting CO₂ emissions in Bangladesh with a Temporal Fusion Transformer
projects.summary: Temporal Fusion Transformer modelling of Bangladesh’s annual carbon-emission series.
projects.problem: Forecast Bangladesh’s carbon emissions using the available historical time series.
projects.approach: Used annual Global Carbon Atlas observations from 1960–2021 and a Temporal Fusion Transformer, with temporal features and a quantile-based forecasting objective.
projects.outcome: The study led to the Forecasting Carbon Footprint conference paper in the ICICDS proceedings.

projects.title: Prediction, transform coding, and entropy coding
projects.summary: Spatial prediction, DCT/KLT experiments, and a Huffman–arithmetic coding comparison.
projects.problem: Examine how prediction, transforms, and entropy coding contribute to a compression pipeline.
projects.approach: Compared image and residual entropy, spatial predictors including MED, DCT/KLT representations, Huffman codeword lengths, and an implemented arithmetic bitstream coder.
projects.outcome: The report records successful arithmetic decoding for all tested symbol streams and compares sample payload lengths against empirical entropy.
projects.context: The coding comparison measures symbol payloads, excluding headers and probability models. Arithmetic streams were decoded and checked; Huffman lengths were computed from the code tree.
sources: DT096A_Lab2_Editable_Report.docx, coding comparison and scope notes

projects.title: Daily sales forecasting in a supershop
projects.summary: Hybrid linear-regression and XGBoost forecasting of daily supermarket sales.
projects.problem: Predict future sales to support supermarket inventory decisions.
projects.approach: Compared linear regression, random forest, and XGBoost with hybrid models that combine a linear trend with residual prediction. The paper describes 211 training days and a 90-day test period.
projects.outcome: The linear-regression–XGBoost model achieved MAE 68.94, RMSE 77.48, and MAPE 0.09 in the published evaluation.

projects.title: Retail hyperautomation: forecasting, placement, and a voice bot
projects.summary: Hybrid sales forecasting, association-rule mining, and a voice interface for supermarket operations.
projects.problem: Explore machine-learning approaches to product demand, product placement, and customer queries in a supermarket.
projects.approach: Investigated a hybrid linear regression–XGBoost forecasting model, compared association-rule mining algorithms including FP-Growth, and developed a voice bot using NLP and speech tools.
projects.outcome: The published study reports linear–XGBoost MAE of 68.94, RMSE of 77.48, and MAPE of 0.09. It also reports an FP-Growth runtime of 0.473 seconds for category-level rules at minimum support 0.03.
